title: Non-Payment Timeline Figures by HomeShield Program
content:
Homeowners Insurance billing under the HomeShield programs runs on four program figures when an installment goes unpaid. All periods are counted in calendar days.

| Program | Grace period after an installment due date before a non-payment notice is sent | Notice period between the non-payment notice and cancellation | Reinstatement window after a non-payment cancellation | Reinstatement fee (USD) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| HomeShield Essential | 10 days | 10 days | 15 days | 25.00 |
| HomeShield Standard | 10 days | 10 days | 15 days | 25.00 |
| HomeShield Plus | 10 days | 10 days | 30 days | 25.00 |
| HomeShield Preferred | 15 days | 10 days | 30 days | 15.00 |
| HomeShield Premier | 15 days | 10 days | 30 days | 15.00 |
| HomeShield Estate | 20 days | 10 days | 30 days | 0.00 |

## What the figures measure

- **Grace period**: calendar days after an installment due date before a non-payment notice is sent.
- **Notice period**: calendar days of notice between the non-payment notice and cancellation. It is 10 days in every program.
- **Reinstatement window**: calendar days after a non-payment cancellation within which the policy may be reinstated.
- **Reinstatement fee**: the fee, in dollars, to reinstate after a non-payment cancellation. Under HomeShield Estate it is 0.00 dollars.

## Reading across the programs

The grace period lengthens with the program: 10 days for HomeShield Essential, Standard and Plus, 15 days for HomeShield Preferred and Premier, and 20 days for HomeShield Estate. The reinstatement window is 15 days for HomeShield Essential and Standard and 30 days for every program from HomeShield Plus upward. The reinstatement fee is 25.00 dollars for HomeShield Essential, Standard and Plus, 15.00 dollars for HomeShield Preferred and Premier, and nothing under HomeShield Estate.
